findings.title: DROP_ACTIVE kill switch bypass — admin toggle does not gate checkout
findings.location: src/lib/config/store.ts (isDropActive reads env var) vs src/routes/(admin)/admin/dashboard/+page.server.ts (toggleStoreStatus writes DB settings row); checkout at src/routes/api/create-checkout-session/+server.ts:31
findings.attack: Operator pauses store in admin dashboard; settings.drop_active becomes 'false' and UI shows paused. Customers still POST /api/create-checkout-session successfully because isDropActive() reads the DROP_ACTIVE env var, which is unchanged.
findings.impact: Orders and Stripe payments continue during a state the operator believes is closed. Defeats the documented kill switch (explicit security boundary). Fulfillment chaos, oversell risk, incident-response failure.
findings.fix: Make isDropActive() read settings.drop_active from SQLite (single source of truth), or have the admin toggle update the env-backed value. Reconcile the two sources.

findings.title: Admin session cookie stores the raw passcode
findings.location: src/routes/(admin)/admin/+page.server.ts: cookies.set(COOKIE_NAME, ADMIN_PASSCODE, ...); isAuthenticated compares cookies.get(COOKIE_NAME) === ADMIN_PASSCODE
findings.attack: Any non-JS exfiltration of the cookie (proxy logs, request mirroring, server-side header logging, backups) yields the long-lived admin passcode directly, since the token equals the credential.
findings.impact: Single cookie leak = full admin takeover persisting until env var rotation. Combined with F-3 (weak default admin123, no rate limit) this is trivially exploitable.
findings.fix: Store a random, revocable session id in the cookie; validate server-side. Never store the raw credential as the session token.

findings.title: No rate limiting/lockout on admin login + weak default passcode
findings.attack: Unthrottled POST /admin with FormData passcode guesses. Non-constant-time !== compare. admin123 is dictionary-brute-forceable in seconds.
findings.impact: Full admin takeover: inventory CRUD, order deletion, store toggle, disclosure of all customer emails and order history.
findings.fix: Constant-time compare, per-IP rate limit on /admin login, lockout after N failures, require strong generated passcode (or magic-link auth).

findings.title: X-Forwarded-For spoofing bypasses waitlist rate limit + O(n) memory amplification
findings.location: src/routes/api/waitlist/+server.ts extractIp(); src/lib/server/waitlist.ts isDuplicate() and addToWaitlist()
findings.attack: Send POST /api/waitlist with a unique X-Forwarded-For and unique email per request. Rate limit (3/hr) never trips. isDuplicate reads the whole file O(n); addToWaitlist reads it again for the pair-assert. Two full reads per request on an unboundedly growing file.
findings.impact: Rate limit defeated; waitlist polluted with arbitrary emails; O(n) per request enables memory exhaustion DoS from a single client.
findings.fix: Trust XFF only from a known proxy hop (use getClientAddress behind a trusted proxy). Drop the post-write pair-assert readback on the hot path. Cap file size or move to SQLite.

findings.title: Payment captured but order rejected on stock race — no automatic refund
findings.location: src/routes/api/create-checkout-session/+page.server.ts pre-check; src/routes/api/webhooks/stripe/+server.ts OUT_OF_STOCK branch returns 200 with no refund
findings.attack: Two customers check out the last unit near-simultaneously. Both Stripe Checkout Sessions are created (stock pre-check passes for both). Both pay. Webhook decrements stock for the first; second hits OUT_OF_STOCK, returns HTTP 200, payment is captured, no stripe.refunds.create anywhere in repo.
findings.impact: Customer pays for an order that will never be fulfilled; no automatic refund; chargeback/dispute risk; operator receives no alert (only console.warn).
findings.fix: Issue stripe.refunds.create on OUT_OF_STOCK in the webhook and email the operator. Optionally reserve stock at session-creation time with a TTL.

findings.title: Order audit log not gitignored; path mismatch with README
findings.location: src/lib/server/logger.ts writes join(process.cwd(), 'orders.log.jsonl'); .gitignore omits orders.log.jsonl, data/waitlist.jsonl, data/orders.jsonl
findings.attack: Developer runs store locally, then git add . — customer PII (emails, shipping addresses, recipient names) lands in git history.
findings.impact: PII disclosure via committed git history if pushed.
findings.fix: Write to data/orders.jsonl (match README) and add data/*.jsonl and orders.log.jsonl to .gitignore.
